title: Z-RAM revived: SiGe quantum-well hole trap on bulk silicon
idea: Z-RAM died because holes stored in an SOI floating body leaked out through the junctions within milliseconds, and SOI wafers cost too much. Bury a 5-8 nm Si0.6Ge0.4 layer under a bulk vertical channel: its ~0.3-0.4 eV valence-band offset forms a hole well that keeps stored holes away from junction fields, and a p+ counter-doped floor isolates the body with no SOI.
why: Capacitorless 1T cell (~4F2) with an estimated 10-100x Z-RAM retention; removes the capacitor charge wall (Fact 1) and the SOI wafer cost; Ge is not a chokepoint.

title: TSRAM fixed: hBN monolayer barriers make tunnel-diode latches reproducible
idea: TI's tunneling SRAM and 1960s Esaki-diode memories died because peak current depends exponentially on barrier thickness, so a one-monolayer deposition error broke the latch. Build each resonant-tunneling diode from an hBN/graphene/hBN stack whose barrier thickness is an integer layer count. A Goto pair of two series RTDs then holds a static bit at nA holding current with no capacitor.
why: Refresh-free static cell of ~8-10F2 vs SRAM's ~120F2; removes refresh energy (Fact 3) and the capacitor (Fact 1); variability is set by quantized layer count, not deposition drift.

title: Bubble memory without the shift register: one garnet bubble per cell
idea: Magnetic bubble memory died from serial millisecond access and external rotating-field coils. Pattern ~40 nm insulating TmIG garnet dots under a Pt strip: a spin-orbit-torque pulse nucleates or annihilates one bubble domain in place, and spin-Hall magnetoresistance in the same Pt reads it, so nothing moves and no tunnel barrier exists to wear out.
why: Random access in ~10 ns, nonvolatile (zero refresh), no barrier breakdown so endurance is not oxide-limited; insulating magnet means no electromigration. Risk: small SMR read signal.

title: Memristor without filaments: conducting ferroelectric domain walls in LiNbO3
idea: HPE's TiO2 memristor died from random oxygen-vacancy filaments that caused variability, sneak paths and ~1e6-1e9 endurance. Replace the filament with a charged, conducting domain wall in a thin-film LiNbO3 mesa: writing nucleates or erases the wall deterministically at a lithographic edge, and a sub-coercive read senses wall conduction between side electrodes without moving it.
why: Deterministic, non-destructive read; endurance >1e12 because no ions migrate; ~1e3 on/off. Attacks destructive read (Fact 8) and refresh (Fact 3).

title: Optane endurance fix: monatomic antimony that cannot segregate
idea: Optane cells wore out after ~1e7-1e8 cycles as Ge, Sb and Te segregated and voids formed during repeated melt-quench. Use pure Sb confined to a 3-4 nm film inside a carbon/SiN pore: a single element has nothing to segregate, and nanoconfinement keeps the amorphous phase stable.
why: Endurance pushed toward 1e12+ with lower reset energy from the thinner film, keeping the 4F2 stacked crosspoint density.

title: Ramtron FeRAM read without destroying: second-harmonic polarization sensing
idea: Ramtron FeRAM was hobbled by destructive reads that forced a write-back on every access and drove fatigue. Read instead with a small sub-coercive AC tone (~0.2 Vc): the sign of the capacitor's second-harmonic current, from its asymmetric C-V curvature, flips with polarization direction, so a lock-in style sense amp reads the bit without switching it.
why: Non-destructive read removes write-back energy and read fatigue (Fact 8): ~2-5x lower read energy and effectively unlimited read endurance.

title: 3D core memory: deposited magnetic rings threaded by vertical vias
idea: Core memory died because millimetre ferrite cores had to be threaded by hand. Deposit alternating CoFeB-ring/dielectric tiers as 3D NAND does and etch one vertical metal pillar through each ring stack: coincident currents in the pillar and a tier plate line flip one ring's vortex chirality, and a TMR sensor on each tier reads it.
why: 3D density from one etch with no lateral transistor per tier (Fact 2); nonvolatile, and closed-flux rings do not couple even at tight pitch.

title: Cavendish NEMS fixed: contactless bistable buckled nanobeams
idea: Cavendish Kinetics' MEMS memory died from contact stiction and wear. Use a compressively pre-stressed SiN or TiN nanobeam (~1 um x 20 nm) that Euler-buckles up or down: side electrodes snap it between the two stable shapes without it touching anything, and a capacitive or piezoresistive pickoff reads which way it bows.
why: No contact means no stiction or wear (endurance 1e15+ plausible); nonvolatile mechanical state with zero leakage or refresh; GHz-class nanobeams switch in ~ns.

title: NRAM with exactly one nanotube junction per cell via DNA origami
idea: Nantero NRAM stalled on random CNT fabrics: a variable number of tube junctions per cell spread the switching distribution, and the feedstock needed costly purification. Use DNA-origami templates anchored in lithographic binding sites to place exactly two crossed CNTs per cell (chirality purity is irrelevant because switching is electromechanical), then strip the DNA with an O2 plasma.
why: Narrow switching distributions at ~20 nm cells; nonvolatile vdW latch with no refresh; the bit element is placed by self-assembly rather than EUV.

title: Zettacore revived: solid-state redox monolayer multiplies capacitor charge
idea: ZettaCore's porphyrin memory died because its redox molecules needed a liquid electrolyte. Tether a ferrocene/porphyrin monolayer to the DRAM storage-node electrode and cap it with an ALD solid ion conductor (LiPON-like): Faradaic charge of 1-4 electrons per molecule adds ~10-30 uC/cm2 of pseudocapacitance on top of the dielectric charge.
why: 3-10x storage charge per area breaks the capacitor wall (Fact 1) without AR 115; shorter pillars save etch steps and collapse risk. Risk: redox kinetics must reach <10 ns.

title: HP rotaxane crossbar fixed: molecular shuttles locked in a MOF lattice
idea: HP/UCLA rotaxane crossbars failed because evaporated top metal punched through the soft monolayer, so the 'switching' was really filaments. Grow a thin rigid metal-organic framework whose linkers are bistable [2]rotaxanes, so each ring shuttles between two stations inside a stiff pore, and laminate a transferred graphene top electrode so no metal atoms enter.
why: Molecular-scale bits (~100 shuttles per cell ensemble), nonvolatile with no refresh, low-temperature and stackable in BEOL.

title: Racetrack without current: VCMA peristaltic domain-wall pumping
idea: IBM's racetrack stalled because moving domain walls needed ~1e7-1e8 A/cm2 and walls pinned randomly. Lay three-phase gate electrodes along a short 16-bit CoFeB/MgO track: sequential voltage-controlled anisotropy waves, a local electrostatic version of bubble memory's rotating field, push every wall one notch per clock with no current through the track.
why: Shift energy drops from pJ to ~fJ per bit (CV2 only); 16 bits per access transistor gives ~2F2/bit and shrinks periphery per bit (Fact 7).

title: Parametron reborn: bits as oscillation phase in pumped nanoresonators
idea: Goto's parametron died because its ferrite-core resonators were big and power-hungry next to transistors. Use GHz AlN nanomechanical resonators parametrically driven by one shared global pump: each holds a 0 or pi oscillation phase indefinitely while the pump runs, is written by a tiny seed pulse and is read by phase comparison.
why: Volatile but leakage-free, so there is no refresh tail (Fact 3) and no row-hammer charge coupling (Fact 9); retention is set by pump stability, not femtoamp leakage. Density limited (~0.1 um2).

title: TAS-MRAM without Joule heating: all-optical GdFeCo writes
idea: Crocus's thermally assisted MRAM died from the energy and time spent Joule-heating cells past the antiferromagnet blocking temperature. Write a GdFeCo ferrimagnetic free layer by helicity-independent all-optical toggle switching instead: a ~100 fs pulse, delivered by a shared on-chip waveguide and a plasmonic antenna per row, flips it, and an MTJ reads it.
why: Writes in <10 ps at ~10-100 fJ with no current through the barrier (no breakdown); one laser is amortized across thousands of cells.

title: Qimonda trench reborn on a separate bonded capacitor wafer
idea: Qimonda's trench DRAM died because deep trenches competed with the transistor for area and thermal budget below 40 nm. Etch 100:1 trenches with porous-Si sidewalls (5-10x area) in a cheap blank carrier wafer, fill them with ALD high-k MIM, then hybrid-bond the carrier face-to-face onto the access-transistor wafer at cell pitch.
why: Decouples capacitance from the transistor process: 2-5x Cs (Fact 1), no pillar leaning, and the carrier needs no EUV (Fact 4). Risk: sub-100 nm bond pitch.

title: Ramtron's capacitor repurposed: antiferroelectric charge-dump DRAM storage node
idea: Ferroelectric capacitors failed in FeRAM because reads were destructive and fatigue accumulated, but DRAM reads are destructive anyway. Use a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric whose field-induced polar phase stores ~15-25 uC/cm2 of extra charge above its switching field and back-switches on read, dumping that charge onto the bitline.
why: 2-4x effective charge per capacitor area at the same height, cutting the needed aspect ratio from ~115 toward ~40 (Fact 1); uses existing ZrO2 ALD tools.

title: Thinfilm polymer FeRAM fixed: proton-transfer organic ferroelectric crystals
idea: Thin Film Electronics' and Intel's PVDF polymer FeRAM died from microsecond switching, half-select disturb and a low Curie point. Grow croconic-acid-type hydrogen-bonded crystals in BEOL vias: they switch by collective proton transfer along H-bond chains (P ~20-30 uC/cm2) and deposit below 150 C, so many tiers can stack.
why: Lead-free nonvolatile layer with a tiny thermal budget for monolithic multi-tier stacks; fast proton switching makes FeRAM DRAM-class.

title: STT-MRAM write current cut by orbital torque from light metals
idea: STT-MRAM's bid to replace DRAM (Hynix/Toshiba, Spin Memory) died because the write current needed a big access transistor and broke down the MgO. Drive the free layer with orbital-Hall torque from a Cr or oxidized-Cu underlayer, converted to spin at a thin Ni interface; orbital Hall conductivity can exceed Pt's without Pt or tungsten.
why: ~3-5x lower write current enables a minimum-size access transistor and a ~10-15F2 cell; no current crosses the barrier; avoids the tungsten chokepoint.

title: Unity CMOx fixed: swap slow oxygen ions for nanosecond protons
idea: Unity Semiconductor's CMOx, which exchanged oxygen ions between oxide layers, died from slow, high-voltage switching. Shuttle protons instead, through a phosphosilicate-glass electrolyte into a WO3 channel: high-field proton insertion has shown ns programming, and conductance is read without disturbance.
why: ns low-energy writes with analog multi-level states (2-4 bits per cell gives density); BEOL-compatible.

title: MeRAM timing fixed with NMR-style composite write pulses
idea: Inston's voltage-controlled MeRAM stalled because precessional VCMA switching needs pulse widths exact to ~50 ps, and the anisotropy spread from cell to cell caused write errors. Borrow NMR composite pulses: a three-segment voltage sequence (90-180-90 equivalent precession angles) whose errors cancel to first order in both pulse width and anisotropy.
why: Write error rate from ~1e-3 to <1e-9 at ~fJ voltage-driven writes, making a nonvolatile ~1 fJ/bit DRAM substitute practical.

title: Optane's crosspoint kept, PCM swapped for selector-gated capacitor
idea: Optane died largely on cost and PCM endurance, but its stacked crosspoint and OTS selector worked. Place a tiny MIM capacitor in series with the OTS at each crosspoint: the selector's threshold snap acts as a transistor-free access device, turning the array into a refreshed 4F2 multi-deck DRAM.
why: 4F2 per deck with stackable decks and no lateral transistor (Fact 2); reuses idle chalcogenide PVD tooling. Risk: OTS sub-threshold leakage must reach ~fA.

title: Graveyard harvest fund for dead storage-element IP and engineers
idea: Systematically acquire lapsed or abandoned storage-element patent families (Z-RAM, T-RAM/VLT, Unity CMOx, Spin Memory PSC, Qimonda trench) and rehire their device engineers. Run each through a 'name the killer, fix only the killer' gate with a 90-day test-chip budget.
why: Starts on a decade of sunk R&D at pennies on the dollar, cutting time to first silicon by an estimated 2-4 years (capital and time axis).

title: Straintronics unclamped: remanent ferroelastic strain read by MoS2 gauge
idea: Straintronic memories stalled because substrate clamping cut piezo strain to ~1e-4, too little to switch magnets reliably. Drop the magnet: store the bit as a 71/109-degree ferroelastic domain state in a BiFeO3 or PMN-PT island, which holds ~0.1-0.5% remanent strain, and read it through a monolayer MoS2 channel on top whose strain-shifted bandgap changes its current several-fold.
why: Nonvolatile, written by field (fJ-class charge) with a non-destructive read and no current through any storage barrier.

title: 1952 BaTiO3 crossbar redone in AlScN: square loop, Tc >1000 C
idea: Bell Labs' 1952 BaTiO3 matrix memory failed because its rounded loop let half-select pulses disturb neighbours, and its ~120 C Curie point sits right at 125 C. Wurtzite Al0.7Sc0.3N switches through nucleation-limited, very square loops (Ec ~3-5 MV/cm), so a passive V/3 crossbar is disturb-free, and its polarization is safe far above 125 C because its Tc exceeds 1000 C.
why: Transistor-free stackable crosspoint FeRAM that qualifies at Grade 1 (125 C/10 y); ~4F2 per layer; lead-free, sputtered with CMOS-compatible tools.

title: Fairchild CCD memory reborn as vertical IGZO buried-channel CCD
idea: 1970s CCD memories died from serial access and silicon dark current that filled potential wells within ms when hot. Stack 64-128 gate tiers 3D-NAND-style around a vertical IGZO channel, store electron packets under alternate gates and shift a few stages to a top sense node. IGZO has no holes to invert the channel and a ~3.1 eV gap, so thermal generation stays negligible at 125 C and packets last seconds or more.
why: 3D DRAM with no capacitor and no per-tier transistor (Fact 2), ~10x bits per litho layer; retention far beyond 64 ms even at 125 C.

title: Optane's 85 C ceiling raised by a tensile cage around amorphous GST
idea: Optane-class PCM was rated for only ~85 C retention because amorphous GST crystallizes when hot. The amorphous phase is ~6-8% less dense than the crystal, so wrap each cell in a pre-stressed SiN/TiN liner that holds its volume in tension; tension penalizes the denser crystal and should raise the effective crystallization barrier by ~0.2-0.4 eV.
why: Pushes 10-year retention past 125 C without Ge-rich alloys that slow writes, keeping ~100 ns PCM speed for automotive and industrial memory.

title: Kilopass VLT thyristor fixed in GaN: standby current vanishes when hot
idea: T-RAM and Kilopass's VLT thyristor DRAM died because latch holding and leakage currents scale with the intrinsic carrier density ni, which explodes at high temperature in silicon. Grow the vertical p-n-p-n in GaN-on-Si (Eg 3.4 eV, ni ~1e-10 cm-3): off-state leakage and holding-current drift sit many orders of magnitude below silicon at 125 C while the cell stays a ~4F2 static latch.
why: Refresh-free static cell at Grade 1 temperature with negligible standby power; uses existing 300 mm GaN-on-Si lines.

title: Optane without melting: MnTe crystal-to-crystal polymorph switching
idea: Optane's melt-quench writes burned energy, and its amorphous state drifted and recrystallized when hot. Switch MnTe between its NiAs-type and wurtzite-type crystalline polymorphs through a displacive transition with no melting: both states are crystals, so neither drifts nor crystallizes at 125 C, and the polymorphs show a large reported resistance contrast.
why: 10-year retention above 125 C with an estimated 3-10x lower write energy than melting and no resistance drift, so multi-level storage becomes viable.

title: Ramtron imprint beaten by periodic data-polarity inversion
idea: PZT FeRAM lost margin at high temperature because a polarization held one way for years imprints: defect dipoles align and the loop shifts. Every few days at 125 C, a background engine rewrites each row inverted and toggles a per-row polarity flag, so no domain spends more than about half its life in one direction and imprint averages out.
why: Removes the dominant 125 C/10 y FeRAM failure mode at ~1e-6 duty-cycle energy; works with any ferroelectric (HZO, AlScN, PZT).

title: Dense MRAM's heat-and-crosstalk wall broken by antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions
idea: Early dense-MRAM efforts lost thermal stability at small sizes and high temperature, and stray fields coupled neighbouring bits. Store the bit in the magnetic-octupole order of noncollinear antiferromagnetic Mn3Pt (TN ~475 K), read through an all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junction: exchange-enhanced anisotropy and zero net moment give Delta > 60 at 125 C in a 20 nm cell with no stray-field crosstalk.
why: Grade-1 retention at sub-20 nm pitch; ps-scale antiferromagnetic dynamics allow fast SOT writes; no inter-cell coupling raises density.

title: DX centers rescued: deep-defect bistability in Si-doped AlN
idea: Persistent-photoconductivity DX-center memories in AlGaAs died because the capture barrier (~0.2-0.3 eV) held states only below ~100 K. In AlN:Si or beta-Ga2O3:Si some calculations put the DX configurational barrier near 1 eV, so an ensemble of ~1000 DX centers in a gate layer could be toggled between shallow-donor and negatively charged DX states by hot-electron injection, shifting a transistor threshold that holds at 125 C.
why: A new charge-plus-lattice-relaxation storage mode with no oxide-trap wear; nonvolatile at Grade 1 for a dense gain-cell variant.

title: Cr2O3 magnetoelectric memory's 34 C Neel point swapped for BiFeO3
idea: Voltage-controlled exchange-bias memories built on Cr2O3 stalled because its Neel temperature (~307 K) is below normal operation, let alone 125 C. Use La-doped BiFeO3 (TN ~640 K, Tc ~1100 K): a 100-200 mV pulse switches its ferroelectric polarization, which rotates the antiferromagnetic axis and, through exchange, a CoFe free layer read by an MTJ.
why: ~1 fJ current-free writes with magnetic order stable at 125 C/10 y; a nonvolatile DRAM-class cell in MESO style.

title: Williams tube's ghost: vacuum-nanogap access switch for temperature-proof retention
idea: Tube memories died from heaters, size and drift, but vacuum isolates charge perfectly. Gate each storage node with a 10-20 nm vacuum-gap field-emission switch carved in the BEOL and sealed at wafer level: its off-current is Fowler-Nordheim tunneling, essentially temperature-independent, not thermionic or generation leakage, so the femtoamp tail does not grow at 125 C.
why: Temperature-flat retention removes the ~8x refresh penalty silicon DRAM pays at 125 C (Fact 3); no channel material means no PBTI drift.

title: Widrow's memistor revived: thermally gated oxide-ion bit
idea: Widrow's 1960 memistor, copper plated from a liquid electrolyte, died from slowness and liquids. Use a solid oxide-ion conductor (stabilized zirconia, Ea ~1.0-1.1 eV) between mixed-conducting electrodes, with an integrated nanoheater that takes the 20 nm cell to ~700 C during writes: ions move ~1 nm in ~100 ns when hot, while diffusion at 125 C is roughly ten orders of magnitude slower.
why: Ionic memory whose 125 C/10 y retention follows directly from high activation energy; multi-level; mostly earth-abundant Zr.

title: Thinfilm PVDF fixed: vapor-deposited aromatic polyurea ferroelectric
idea: Printed PVDF-TrFE FeRAM (Thinfilm, Opticom) died partly because its ~100-130 C Curie point and slow switching ruled out hot or fast use. Vapor-deposition-polymerize an aromatic polyurea whose urea dipoles lock into H-bonded sheets that stay polar above ~200 C, coating 3D trenches conformally at room temperature.
why: An organic nonvolatile layer stable at 125 C/10 y, deposited at room temperature for monolithic many-tier stacks, with no ALD or EUV for the storage layer.

title: Nanocrystal variability ended: atomically identical molybdenum polyoxometalate charge nodes
idea: Freescale's silicon-nanocrystal memories and Hitachi's few-electron PLEDM died from dot-to-dot size and charge variability. Graft monodisperse Mo- or V-based polyoxometalate clusters, every one atomically identical, multi-electron redox-active and stable above 400 C, as discrete storage nodes over a 2-3 nm tunnel oxide; choosing Mo/V instead of the usual tungsten POMs dodges the W chokepoint.
why: Zero size variability with quantized multi-bit charge levels and 125 C robustness; ~1e13 nodes/cm2.

title: CBRAM's hot-retention killer fixed by intermetallic-compound filaments
idea: Adesto/Crossbar Ag and Cu filaments dissolved at 125 C because a few-atom metallic chain has high surface energy and diffuses away. Switch in an amorphous Ge-Te or Si-Te matrix where injected Cu reacts into a Cu2Te or Cu3Ge compound filament, a thermodynamic minimum rather than a metastable chain, and reset it by field-driven decomposition.
why: Moves CBRAM retention from ~85 C to Grade 1 while keeping ns low-voltage writes in a dense crosspoint.

title: HPE memristor's wandering vacancies ordered: brownmillerite-perovskite topotactic switching
idea: TiO2 memristors failed hot because disordered oxygen vacancies diffused and filaments relaxed. Use an SrFeO2.5 brownmillerite film whose vacancies sit in ordered channels: a field converts a nanoscale region topotactically to conductive perovskite SrFeO3-d, so the two states are distinct crystal phases separated by a structural barrier rather than a diffusing cloud.
why: Phase-distinct states give 125 C/10 y retention with area-type, non-filament switching and low variability.

title: Hot-zone beachhead: launch where silicon DRAM hurts most
idea: Nantero, Optane and early MRAM died without a market where they beat DRAM on day one. Launch a 125 C-native storage element first in Grade-1 automotive and industrial LPDDR sockets, where silicon DRAM must refresh ~8x faster and derate, and pre-sell to Tier-1s with 10-year supply contracts that fund the fab ramp.
why: Turns the constraint into a price premium (~1.5-3x $/bit tolerated), funds capital intensity from early revenue and builds U.S. volume.

title: Qualification by kinetic-crossover hunting, not single-Arrhenius extrapolation
idea: Several dead memories (early PCM, CBRAM) passed high-temperature bakes but failed in the field because a second, lower-activation-energy failure path dominated at use conditions. Require bakes at five temperatures (125-250 C) plus Kissinger ramp analysis to detect kinetic crossover, and design storage elements with at least 0.3 eV margin between competing mechanisms.
why: Prevents the late qualification failures that kill ventures and makes the 125 C/10 y guarantee credible early in development.

title: STT barrier wear-out turned self-healing with spinel MgAl2O4
idea: STT-MRAM as DRAM failed partly because write currents build oxygen-vacancy traps in MgO until breakdown (~1e10-1e12 cycles). Use a lattice-matched spinel MgAl2O4 barrier, cation-disorder engineered so vacancy traps anneal out at 125 C or below within hours, so a hot ambient repairs the barrier faster than writes damage it.
why: Turns 125 C from a stressor into a continuous healing anneal, potentially lifting endurance toward 1e15 for DRAM-class duty.

title: NRAM's van der Waals idea, crystallized: sliding-ferroelectric bilayer bit
idea: NRAM's insight, a nanoscale state latched by van der Waals energy far above kT, was undone by random CNT fabrics. Keep the vdW latch but make it crystalline: a rhombohedral-stacked bilayer h-BN or 3R-MoS2 whose out-of-plane polarization flips when the layers slide by one bond length under a gate field, a lattice-locked stacking state that holds above 125 C.
why: Fatigue-free sliding switching with no ion displacement, an atomically thin nonvolatile cell at Grade 1, read via the threshold shift of an adjacent 2D channel.

title: STT-DRAM's shrinking-Delta killer fixed with tall shape-anisotropy free layers
idea: Samsung and Hynix STT-MRAM DRAM-replacement efforts stalled because interfacial anisotropy cannot keep Delta >= 60 at sub-20 nm diameters and 125 C. Make the free layer a 20-40 nm tall CoFeB/FeCo cylinder (aspect ratio >1.5), so perpendicular shape anisotropy, which falls only slowly with temperature, supplies the stability.
why: 125 C/10 y retention at ~10-15 nm diameter: 2-4x density over interfacial-PMA MTJs.

title: Mercury relays shrunk: sealed Galinstan nanodroplet electrocapillary bit
idea: Mercury-wetted relays and mercury delay lines died from toxicity and size. Seal a ~50 nm gallium-alloy droplet in a two-well SiO2 nanochannel and shift it between wells with an electrocapillary pulse, bridging or opening a read electrode pair; liquid metal neither wears nor fatigues and stays liquid and stable from -19 C to above 1000 C.
why: Nonvolatile resistive bit with ~1e6 on/off and no wear-out mechanism, stable at 125 C/10 y; speed set by nanoscale capillary times (est. 10-100 ns).

title: Bubble-memory precedent: federal rugged-memory purchase guarantee for domestic production
idea: Magnetic bubble memory survived years longer because U.S. military and aerospace buyers needed rugged storage. Replicate that with a DoD/DOE/automotive consortium that guarantees purchase of at least 10M units per year of a 125 C/10 y-qualified, U.S.-fabbed DRAM-class element for five years, paid only after qualification.
why: Demand certainty lowers capital risk for the first U.S. line, lifting U.S. manufacturability above today's ~1-2% share.

title: YMnO3 FeFET retried: improper ferroelectric resists depolarization when hot
idea: Late-1990s YMnO3 FeFETs died from leakage, charge injection and depolarization-limited retention. Use hexagonal YMnO3, whose polarization is improper (slaved to a lattice trimerization, Tc > 1000 K) so depolarization fields barely back-switch it, on a floating-metal MFMIS gate so the semiconductor never sees an injection field.
why: Keeps polarization at 125 C/10 y where proper ferroelectrics depolarize at scaled thickness, enabling a 1T nonvolatile gain-type cell.
